info.title: StampMitra Developer API
info.summary: Indian identity verification and e-Stamp Paper APIs for the StampMitra developer portal.
info.description:
The API-key Developer Suite: verification (PAN, GSTIN, vehicle RC, Voter ID, Driving Licence, Passport, CIN, Udyam, bank account), e-Stamp Paper, usage and request logs, and webhook events. Generated from the same data as the docs at https://developer.stampmitra.in.

Authentication: send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`. Sandbox keys (sk_test_) and production keys (sk_live_) use the same host; the key prefix selects the environment. Sandbox keys are free and get 20% of each endpoint's production rate limit (minimum 1 request per window); production calls are metered per successful call.

Errors: every error is `{ error: { code, message, requestId } }` (plus `field` where an input is at fault). Send an `X-Request-Id` header and it is echoed back as `requestId`. See `x-error-codes`.

Idempotency: send an `Idempotency-Key` header on operations that accept it (metered verification and duty/parties calls, order creation, payment intents) to make retries safe. The same key and request replays the stored response; the same key with a different request is 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; the same key while the first request is still running is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` with `Retry-After`. Keys are scoped to your organization, the route and the environment and are kept for 24 hours. `x-idempotent` and `x-retry-safe` mark each operation.

Response headers on authenticated calls (additive, safe to ignore): `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds) on rate-limited routes, `Retry-After` on every 429 and 503, and for live keys `X-Wallet-State` (OK, LOW_BALANCE, FINISHED) and `X-Wallet-Balance-Low: true`. Read the exact balance with GET /v1/account/balance; guide: https://developer.stampmitra.in/docs/balance-usage-and-rate-limits.

Webhooks: outbound order events are signed. `x-webhook-signature` and the top-level `webhooks` section describe the headers and the HMAC-SHA256 construction.

Versioning: Contract version (info.version) follows semantic versioning, independent of the URL version (x-api-version: v1; every path is under /v1). MAJOR: any breaking change to the published contract (removed or renamed operationId, path, field or enum value; changed status code, error shape or required-ness; a /v2 prefix). Generated SDKs bump their major version too. MINOR: backwards-compatible additions (new endpoint, new optional request field, new response field, new error code or webhook event). Clients must ignore unknown response fields and treat unknown enum values as unknown-safe. PATCH: documentation, description and example corrections that do not change behaviour.

servers.description: StampMitra Developer API. Sandbox and production share this host: use an sk_test_ key for sandbox (free, lower rate limits) and an sk_live_ key for production.

x-error-codes.description: Validation failed or the request was rejected, or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED: the route requires an Idempotency-Key header (e-Stamp order creation, batches).
Missing or invalid API key, or missing required scope.
IP not allowed, plan entitlement not enabled, or limit reached.
State conflict, or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS: a request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed (retry the identical request after Retry-After).
Request understood but cannot be processed, or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED: the Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.
Unexpected error, and upstream failures (502, 503). The status distinguishes them.

x-webhook-signature.secret: The signing secret of the webhook endpoint you registered.

get.summary: List entitled services (generic catalog, covers e-Stamp services too)
get.description: Returns every service (verification AND e-Stamp) this organization is entitled to. There is no e-Stamp-specific catalog endpoint yet; e-Stamp instruments surface here as regular service entries once entitled.
Detail for a single serviceCode, if entitled and active.

get.summary: Get the e-Stamp input field schema
get.description: Generic form-rendering metadata for the e-Stamp product. `serviceCode` is accepted for forward-compatible route shape parity with other schema lookups; e-Stamp has exactly one schema regardless of its value. Requires the `estamp.read` scope.
Served from StampMitra's synced master-data catalogue. Requires the `estamp.read` scope.
There is no separate instrument entity distinct from an article - this returns the same state-scoped article catalogue as the articles endpoint below. Requires the `estamp.read` scope.
`instrumentCode` is treated as a state code here - there is no article sub-breakdown below the state-scoped list. Requires the `estamp.read` scope.

post.summary: Calculate authoritative e-Stamp duty + service charges
post.description: Runs the one authoritative pricing calculation; the response amount is never recalculated or overridden client-side. Requires the `estamp.duty.calculate` scope. Metered against your fulfilment wallet.

201.description: Success, same body as 200. The backend documents 200 but NestJS defaults POST handlers to 201, so clients must accept any 2xx.

post.description: Attaches or corrects the customer/party details on an existing e-Stamp order. Requires the `estamp.parties.write` scope. Metered against your fulfilment wallet.

201.description: Success, same body as 200. The backend documents 200 but NestJS defaults POST handlers to 201, so clients must accept any 2xx.

post.summary: Create an order (generic - works for any entitled serviceCode, including e-Stamp)
post.description: Generic order-creation endpoint. For e-Stamp, pass an e-Stamp `serviceCode` (from GET /v1/services) and put instrument/party/value details in the free-form `details` object. There is no e-Stamp-specific request/response contract yet (no first-class `state`, `article`, `parties[]` fields) - the shape of `details` for e-Stamp is not finalized upstream.

get.description: Current billing period totals, calls by service, calls by day and a 6-month calls-by-period trend for the organization that owns the API key.

Your wallet balance in rupees and paise, the low-balance threshold (Rs 500 by default), the state (OK, LOW_BALANCE, FINISHED), how many calls it covers at the cheapest approved price and at your 7-day average price, the last top-up and the signup credit still left. Any key with a verification scope can read its own organization's balance. A sandbox key gets a sandbox notice and zero amounts, never a real balance. Rate limit: 60 per minute per key. Amounts exclude GST.

get.summary: Usage this month and last month, with limits
get.description: Current and previous calendar month in IST: requests, billed requests, failed-not-billed, spend before GST, a per-product breakdown and a per-day series, plus today against your limits (requests per minute and per day). A sandbox key sees its own sandbox usage with zero spend. Rate limit: 60 per minute per key.
Paginated request-log listing for the organization that owns the API key. Use nextCursor to fetch the next page.

post.description: Re-fires a specific webhook delivery attempt: the exact same payload through the same delivery path.

Delivered to an endpoint you registered when the order event ORDER_CREATED occurs. Verify X-Webhook-Signature before trusting the body, and respond with any 2xx to acknowledge. A non-2xx response or timeout is retried with exponential backoff (1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 12 h; 6 attempts in total) before the delivery is dead-lettered.

2XX.description: Acknowledged. Any 2xx status marks the delivery as succeeded.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional client-generated key (1 to 255 printable characters) that makes a retried POST safe. A key is scoped to your organization, the route and the environment (a sandbox key never matches a live one) and is kept for 24 hours. Retrying with the same key and the same request replays the original response (same status and body) without repeating the work or billing again. The same key with a different request returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. The same key while the first request is still being processed returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with a Retry-After header. Routes that require the key (POST /v1/estamp/orders, POST /v1/batches) answer 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED without it.

WebhookSignature.name: X-Webhook-Signature
WebhookSignature.description: Hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256(secret, `${timestamp}.${JSON.stringify(payload)}`), where timestamp is the X-Webhook-Timestamp value.

WebhookTimestamp.name: X-Webhook-Timestamp
WebhookTimestamp.description: Unix time in seconds at which this delivery attempt was signed.

WebhookEventId.name: X-Webhook-Event-Id
WebhookEventId.description: Id of this delivery's event; stable across retries, so use it to de-duplicate.
